title: Nvidia-backed Firmus scraps $5 billion Australian IPO as investors step up AI scrutiny
source_used: Reuters, read on the copy site Central Oregon Daily (reuters.com returns 401)
key_facts: Firmus, an Australian data centre operator backed by Nvidia, shelved its $5 billion IPO on Friday 9 Oct 2026 (Sydney dateline) and will seek private funding.
A Nasdaq listing is a possible next step after a private round, a person involved said; the company declined to comment on it.
The IPO would have been the second-largest new share sale in Australian history; demand was lukewarm.
Planned price A$11 a share gave an equity valuation of $30.6 billion, nearly triple the $10.5 billion from a fundraising at the start of August.

Investors worried about the debt pile (about $30 billion per the lead managers' analysts), the lack of a track record building AI data centres, and reports a key partner was pulling out of an A$73 billion development deal.
Investors began pulling orders on Wednesday after CDC Data Centres CEO Greg Boorer said on the Rampart podcast the 1.6 gigawatt plan with Firmus was no longer underway.
Investors were also put off by escrow terms that would have let existing holders sell over half the stock from day one.
Fund manager Jun Bei Liu called it an important reality check but not the beginning of the end of the AI trade.
quote_evidence: Australia's Firmus, a data centre operator backed by Nvidia, shelved its $5 billion initial public offering on Friday, opting for a private fundraising round ahead of a potential New York share sale.

Firmus' IPO would have been the second-largest new share sale in Australia's history but met lukewarm demand, a warning sign that investors remain selective about AI issuers even as the artificial intelligence boom drives global markets.
Firmus considered cutting the issue price to entice more investors, one of the people involved in the deal said, but opted instead to look towards a private funding round.
why_it_matters_hint: A $5 billion AI-infrastructure listing failed for lack of demand, a test of how much investors will pay for AI data-centre companies.
notes: Reuters original returns 401; text of the Reuters story read on Central Oregon Daily (wire copy), cross-checked with ABC News Australia (same facts: float withdrawn, private funding, CDC split). Continues our 6 Oct 2026 item (CDC and Firmus ending Project Southgate).
